matchstick.title: Check arithmetic validity
matchstick.principle: After proposing a transformed equation, compute the integer values of both sides using standard Roman numeral rules to ensure the equality holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you have a candidate transformed equation, before finalizing, evaluate both sides numerically.
matchstick.example: Accepting a transformed equation without verifying that the left and right side values match, leading to a false equality.

matchstick.title: Match‑stick orientation matters
matchstick.principle: A stick’s orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) is fixed; you may only place it in a location that matches its orientation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When moving a stick, ensure the destination character expects a stick of the same orientation.
matchstick.example: Turning an I (vertical) into a V by moving the vertical stick to a diagonal position, creating an invalid numeral.

matchstick.title: Limit changes to two characters
matchstick.principle: A single stick move can affect at most the source character (which loses a stick) and the destination character (which gains a stick).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When planning a move, verify that only two characters change and no other parts of the equation are altered.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from one numeral and inadvertently altering a third character, breaking the puzzle constraints.

matchstick.title: Transform numerals via single stick moves
matchstick.principle: Use known one‑stick transformations (e.g., I↔II, V↔X) that keep both source and destination characters valid Roman numerals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a numeral needs to change by adding or removing a single stick, apply a standard transformation that yields a valid numeral.
matchstick.example: Changing a V to an X by moving a diagonal stick without ensuring the resulting shape is a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final output must be a single line that starts with ‘Correct version of the equation:’ followed by the corrected equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the end of solving, format the answer exactly as required before submitting.
matchstick.example: Providing the corrected equation without the required prefix, causing the answer to be rejected.

matchstick.title: Accurate parsing of the original equation
matchstick.principle: Read the given equation carefully and record each numeral and operator exactly as they appear before attempting any changes.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before any manipulation, parse the equation to identify all numerals and operators.
matchstick.example: Misreading ‘IV’ as ‘VI’, leading to an incorrect transformation.

matchstick.title: Within‑character diagonal repositioning
matchstick.principle: You may relocate a diagonal stick within the same numeral, effectively turning X into V (or V into X) while preserving the stick’s orientation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a numeral contains diagonal sticks and a transformation can be achieved by moving one diagonal within that character.
matchstick.example: Attempting to turn X into V by moving a diagonal to a new position but changing its orientation, resulting in an invalid shape.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion via vertical stick relocation
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to a ‘‑’ creates a ‘+’, and removing the vertical stick from a ‘+’ yields a ‘‑’; the removed stick can be placed elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When an operator needs to change between ‘+’ and ‘‑’, consider moving a vertical stick to or from the operator.
matchstick.example: Changing a ‘+’ to ‘‑’ but forgetting to place the removed vertical stick, effectively deleting a stick.

matchstick.title: Operator swapping via horizontal stick relocation
matchstick.principle: You can move a horizontal stick from the equality sign to a minus sign (or vice versa), turning the ‘=’ into ‘‑’ and the ‘‑’ into ‘=’.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains both ‘=’ and ‘‑’, consider swapping a horizontal stick between them to change their roles.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from ‘=’ to ‘‑’ but leaving the original ‘=’ with only one horizontal, resulting in an invalid operator.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick transfer from '+' to numeral (adds I)
matchstick.principle: When moving a vertical stick from a ‘+’ operator, the ‘+’ becomes ‘‑’, and the removed stick can be added to any numeral that can accept a vertical stick (i.e., to add an extra I), increasing its value by 1. This simultaneous operator conversion and numeral augmentation often resolves the equality.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the equation contains a ‘+’ and a numeral that could be increased by 1 (by adding an I), consider moving the vertical stick from the ‘+’ to that numeral.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from ‘+’ but placing it on a character that cannot accept a vertical stick, creating an invalid numeral.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes a transformed equation is correct without checking the numeric values, leading to false equalities.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always compute the integer values of both sides using Roman numeral rules after any transformation.

matchstick.why_it_happens: When moving sticks, the model may place them in positions that do not correspond to any valid Roman numeral, violating the puzzle constraints.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure that after moving a stick, each character matches a known Roman numeral shape (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) and respects orientation.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may form operators that are not among the allowed set (+, -, =), such as turning ‘=’ into ‘≠’ or creating a non‑standard symbol.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Only use the three allowed operators and verify their stick composition after any move.

matchstick.description: Missing destination for moved stick (effective removal)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick from a source character but does not place it on a valid destination, effectively deleting a stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Every stick move must specify both a source character (which loses a stick) and a destination character (which gains that stick).

matchstick.why_it_happens: The final line does not follow the required prefix or layout, causing the scorer to miss the answer.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Output exactly one line starting with ‘Correct version of the equation:’ followed by the corrected equation, with no extra text.
